source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST API (update_api.rs:49 wait=false) → do_upsert_points → toc.update → Collection.update_from_client (line 140: operation.validate() only checks schema) → shard.update_with_consistency → shard.update → Segment.upsert_point (entry.rs:93: check_named_vectors) → check_vector_against_config (mod.rs:181) where dimension validation ACTUALLY happens
source_grounding.note: Root cause: REST layer validate() (line 36) returns Ok(()) for Single vectors without checking dimension. The actual dimension validation only happens deep in the segment layer (check_vector_against_config). When wait=false, operation is queued and returns 200 BEFORE segment validation runs. When wait=true, segment validation runs synchronously and returns 400. This is a clear validation bypass bug.

verdicts.rationale: Clear validation bypass bug: REST API accepts empty vector (dim 0) when wait=false, returning HTTP 200, but silently discards the data. When wait=true, same request correctly returns 400 with dimension error. Root cause: validate() at REST layer (validate.rs:36) returns Ok(()) for Single vectors without checking dimension. Actual dimension validation only happens deep in segment layer (mod.rs:181 check_vector_against_config), which executes asynchronously when wait=false. This violates the contract that vectors must match collection dimension (proven by wait=true behavior) and creates silent data loss. Matches bug_shape 'parameter_validation-numeric-boundary'. Not a mundane explanation, not by-design, not environment-specific. True bug.
